calibration_of_the_qsar_classifier.caveat: This is the calibration of the classifier on data drawn from its own distribution. It says nothing about the natural-product libraries, which sit outside it -- see the conformal diagnostics (ADR-AIIM-137) for what happens there. The held-out set is also 90.1 % active, so the Brier score must be read against the base-rate predictor rather than against zero.

auc_reconciliation.note: Four numbers, four measurements, none of them wrong. Three appear in the manuscript without being distinguished; the second appears nowhere.

values.what_it_is: Random forest in the four-algorithm screening comparison: nested CV, scaffold-grouped, on the 4,753-compound training portion, with a reduced hyperparameter search (n_iter=6) chosen for tractability across four algorithms.

The retained model's own nested CV on the same 4,753 training compounds, from the run that produced the frozen pipeline. Differs from the line above because it is a separate fit with a fuller search, not a different dataset.

The same frozen model re-evaluated inside the y-randomisation harness, so that the real model and the 100 permuted models are scored by identical code. It is the correct comparator for the permuted mean of 0.500 and is not a fourth estimate of performance.

External performance on the scaffold-disjoint held-out set (n = 1,217). This is the split that doubles as the conformal calibration set, so it is an optimistic estimate -- already declared in Section 2.4.
